---
title: "Solution: Tokenisation and TF-IDF"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidytext)

options(bdat602.source_only = TRUE)
source("courses/bdat-602/_teacher/resources/datasets/simulate_bdat602_data.R")
health_data <- simulate_bdat602(n = 100000, seed = 602)
```

## Task 1: Tokenise complaint notes

```{r task1-tokenise}
complaints <- health_data |>
  filter(!is.na(complaint_notes)) |>
  mutate(doc_id = row_number())

words <- complaints |>
  unnest_tokens(word, complaint_notes)

cat("Total tokens:", nrow(words), "\n")
```

```{r task1-top-raw}
words |>
  count(word, sort = TRUE) |>
  head(20)
# Most frequent raw tokens are stop words: "I", "my", "the", "and", "is"
```

## Task 2: Remove stop words

```{r task2-stop-words}
words_clean <- words |>
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word")

cat("Tokens after stop word removal:", nrow(words_clean), "\n")
```

```{r task2-top-clean}
words_clean |>
  count(word, sort = TRUE) |>
  head(20) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(word, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Top 20 Words in Complaint Notes (after stop word removal)",
       x = "Word", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()
# After removal, insurance domain words dominate: "claim", "premium", "dental", "billing"
```

## Task 3: Compute TF-IDF

```{r task3-tfidf}
word_counts <- words_clean |>
  count(doc_id, word)

tfidf_df <- word_counts |>
  bind_tf_idf(word, doc_id, n)

tfidf_df |>
  arrange(desc(tf_idf)) |>
  head(10)
# High-TF-IDF terms tend to be very specific complaint-level words that appear
# in only one document's template — the simulator uses fixed templates,
# so each term has moderate-to-high TF-IDF across the whole corpus.
```

## Task 4: Top TF-IDF words per complaint category

```{r task4-category}
complaints_cat <- complaints |>
  mutate(category = case_when(
    str_detect(complaint_notes, "billing|premium|deductible|charged|payment|balance") ~ "billing",
    str_detect(complaint_notes, "claim|pending|denied|submitted|approved|documents")  ~ "claims",
    str_detect(complaint_notes, "covered|coverage|prescription|formulary|dental|mental|physiotherapy|doctor") ~ "coverage",
    str_detect(complaint_notes, "customer service|app|portal|hold|transferred|emails|phone") ~ "service",
    TRUE ~ "positive"
  ))

tfidf_cat <- tfidf_df |>
  left_join(complaints_cat |> select(doc_id, category), by = "doc_id")
```

```{r task4-plot}
tfidf_cat |>
  group_by(category, word) |>
  summarise(mean_tfidf = mean(tf_idf), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(category) |>
  slice_max(mean_tfidf, n = 8) |>
  ungroup() |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder_within(word, mean_tfidf, category),
             y = mean_tfidf, fill = category)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~category, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_reordered() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Top TF-IDF Words by Complaint Category",
       x = "Word", y = "Mean TF-IDF") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r task4-interpret}
# The TF-IDF facet plot clearly differentiates the five categories:
# - Billing: "charged", "statement", "premium", "outstanding", "balance"
# - Claims: "claim", "pending", "denied", "documents", "processing"
# - Coverage: "covered", "dental", "prescription", "formulary", "reimbursed"
# - Service: "app", "crashes", "hold", "transferred", "portal"
# - Positive: "satisfied", "professionally", "promptly", "renewed", "clear"
#
# Coverage has the most distinctive vocabulary because it contains very specific
# medical and product terms (formulary, physiotherapy) that do not appear in
# other categories. Billing and claims share some overlap ("claim" is common
# in both contexts), but the top terms still separate them well.
```
